Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain, muscle
tightness, and limited range of motion. The reported symptoms are consistent with the mechanism and force of the impact.
Examination revealed paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced cervical and lumbar motion, while neurological screening,
reflexes, and strength testing were within normal limits. No prior injury or ongoing complaints involving these body regions are
known from the patient's history. Care consisted of 28 visits including manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home exercise
instruction. Treatment followed a typical course, with frequency tapering as pain and mobliity improved and the patient
progressed toward discharge. Billing records relfect single entries for each service with no duplicated charges. Prognosis is good,
with anticipated full resolution of symptoms and return to baseline activity expected within the coming weeks.
